findings.title: Salesforce service references Prisma without importing it
findings.body: The new token-refresh path calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file has no `@calcom/prisma` import. This is an unresolved identifier and prevents the app-store package from type-checking/building.

findings.title: The sync-mode token schema strips the expiry fields needed by consumers
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` does not define a Zod catch-all/index signature; it evaluates to a literal property name such as `[object Object]`. Consequently, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` only retains `access_token` (and strips arbitrary response fields). In credential-sync mode, callers such as Zoom subsequently read `newTokens.expires_in` and calculate `expiry_date` from `undefined`, producing an invalid expiry and causing the credential to remain unusable or the Prisma update to fail. The schema must explicitly accept and preserve the documented expiry field(s), e.g. via `.passthrough()`/`.catchall()` and validation of supported expiry names.

findings.title: Credential-sync refresh returns a different response type than several integrations expect
findings.body: When sync is enabled this helper returns the raw `fetch` `Response`, while its fallback returns whatever each supplied refresh function returns. This breaks integrations whose existing refresh functions return SDK/axios objects rather than a Fetch response. For example, HubSpot casts the result to `HubspotToken` and reads `expiresIn`/`accessToken`, while Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read `.data`; with a Fetch response these fields are absent, so invalid credentials are persisted or token refresh fails. Normalize the sync response to the same contract expected by each caller (or make the helper parse and return a common token payload) before replacing those calls.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends a credential ID as the Cal.com user ID to the sync endpoint
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects its third argument to be the credential owner's user ID and serializes it as `calcomUserId`. This call passes `credentialId`, which is the database credential primary key captured at line 53, not `credential.userId`. A self-hosted credential source will therefore look up the wrong user (or potentially another user whose ID happens to equal that credential ID), making synced Bigin refreshes fail or return the wrong account's token.

findings.title: Outbound token-sync requests contain no authentication
findings.body: The configured credential-sync endpoint is called with only a user ID and app slug; no webhook secret, authorization header, signature, or other credential is sent. If the self-hosted endpoint follows the described contract and returns tokens for these identifiers, anyone who can reach it can request tokens for arbitrary Cal.com user IDs and apps. Require an authenticated request (for example an HMAC signature or the configured shared secret in a header) and document/verify it on the receiving service.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh saves the new token but uses the expired token for the current request
findings.body: The newly added refresh code updates the database with `accessTokenParsed.data`, but the `jsforce.Connection` created immediately afterward still receives `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url`, which are the pre-refresh values. Since this refresh is performed while constructing the service, the first operation after an expired token will authenticate with the expired access token and fail; only a later service instance can use the saved token. Construct the connection from the refreshed response values.
